title: Linking teacher identity with student submissions
description: The grades portal links teacher identity with student submission data through the submission queue, potentially enabling linking of teacher-student relationships through identifiers.
assumptions: Assumes the system uses teacher credentials to access submission queues

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The grades portal processes identified student data (submissions) when displaying the submission queue to teachers, which may include personally identifiable information.
assumptions: Assumes submission data contains student identifiers or other identifying information

title: Collection of more sensitive data than functionally required
description: The submission queue may include more sensitive data types than strictly required for the teacher's review function, such as full student profiles or assessment details beyond what's needed for course review.
assumptions: Assumes the submission queue includes more data than necessary for the stated purpose

title: Data accessible to more parties than functionally necessary
description: Student submission data is made accessible to teachers who may not be functionally required to access all submissions, potentially exceeding the scope of authorized access.
assumptions: Assumes teachers have access to submissions beyond their specific courses

title: Teacher action attribution for submission requests
description: The teacher's login and submission request actions can be attributed to the specific teacher, which may impact non-repudiation of their access to student data.
assumptions: Assumes teacher authentication is used to attribute actions

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The grades portal may process more personal data than actually needed for the functional goal of allowing teachers to review course submissions.
assumptions: Assumes the system collects and processes more data than necessary for the stated purpose

title: Parent-Child Linking via Unique Identifiers
description: Parent account is linked to child account through unique identifiers, enabling linking of parent and child data across the system.
assumptions: Parent account and child account are linked through a unique identifier (e.g., parent-child relationship ID).

title: Quasi-identifier Combining for Parent-Child Linking
description: System combines parent and child attributes (e.g., name, DOB, account ID) to establish parent-child relationship and link data.
assumptions: Parent and child data are combined through quasi-identifiers to establish relationship.

title: Processing of Identified Data (Grades)
description: Grades portal processes identified data (child's grades) which can be linked to specific individuals.
assumptions: Grades are identified data that can be linked to specific child students.

title: Unique Reference to Child Identity
description: Child's grades contain unique references to the identity of the data subject (child student).
assumptions: Grades are associated with unique student identifiers.

title: Revealing Attributes in Parent-Child Relationship
description: Parent-child relationship data includes revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Parent-child relationship includes attributes that can identify the child.

title: Attributable Data Evidence for Parent Access
description: Parent's access to child's grades can be attributed to the parent through authentication records.
assumptions: Parent authentication creates attributable evidence of access.

title: Detection of Grade Access via Observed Communications
description: Access to grades can be detected through observed communications (e.g., login events, data retrieval requests).
assumptions: System logs and monitoring can detect access patterns.

title: Data Type Sensitivity of Grades
description: Grades may be perceived as highly sensitive data and should only be collected and processed when strictly required.
assumptions: Grades are sensitive personal data requiring strict handling.

title: Child's Unawareness of Parent Access
description: Child data subject may not be aware that parent is accessing their grades through the portal.
assumptions: Child may not be informed about parent's access to their academic records.

title: Insufficient Data Subject Controls for Child
description: Child data subject may lack proper controls to access, review, or control their own grade data.
assumptions: Child may not have direct access or control over their grade data.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in grade records
description: Grade records contain unique student identifiers that can be used to link data across different contexts or systems, potentially enabling re-identification of students.
assumptions: Grade records contain student IDs or other unique identifiers

title: Processing of identified data
description: The grading service processes grade records that contain identified information about students, which may include personal identifiers.
assumptions: Grade records contain identifiable student information

title: Identifier in grade records
description: Grade records contain unique references to the identity of the data subject (students), enabling identification of specific individuals.
assumptions: Grade records include student identifiers

title: Data type sensitivity - unnecessary data collection
description: Grade records may contain more sensitive data types than functionally required for building student, parent, and teacher views.
assumptions: Grade records may include unnecessary sensitive fields
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if all grade record fields are necessary for the stated purpose

title: Data exposure to multiple parties
description: Grade records are accessed to build views for students, parents, and teachers - potentially exposing more parties than functionally necessary.
assumptions: Multiple parties (students, parents, teachers) may access the same grade records

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing grade records may involve more personal data than actually needed for the functional goal of building student, parent, and teacher views.
assumptions: Grade records may contain more data than necessary for the stated purpose
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if data minimization is properly implemented
